test.title: Section 3 · why milk is at the back of the shop

texts.title: Why the milk is at the back of the shop

paragraphs.text: Anyone who has gone into a supermarket for a single carton of milk knows the feeling of walking past aisle after aisle to reach it. Many shoppers assume that this is a trick, and to some extent they are right. The layout of a large food shop is one of the most carefully studied spaces in modern life, and very little about it is accidental. Yet the explanations that are usually given are too simple, and some of the most widely repeated claims about supermarket design turn out, on closer inspection, to have little evidence behind them.
paragraphs.label: A

paragraphs.text: The logic starts at the door. Most large shops place fruit, vegetables and flowers near the entrance, because bright colours and fresh smells create an impression of quality that shoppers carry with them through the rest of the visit. Stores also know that people walking in from the street need a few metres to slow down and adjust to their surroundings. Products placed right by the door are often ignored, which is why that area is frequently left open or used for seasonal displays rather than for goods the shop particularly wants to sell. Some stores also change the displays near the entrance every few weeks, so that regular customers notice something new each time they come in.
paragraphs.label: B

paragraphs.text: Everyday essentials such as milk, bread and eggs are usually placed far from the entrance, and the standard explanation is that this forces customers to pass other products on the way. There is some truth in this, but there is also a practical reason that is rarely mentioned. Milk must be kept cold, and the refrigerated cabinets are most easily supplied from the storage and delivery area, which in most buildings is at the back. Putting dairy products along the rear wall shortens the distance that heavy, chilled deliveries have to travel, and reduces the time they spend out of the cold.
paragraphs.label: C

paragraphs.text: Within each aisle, position on the shelf matters more than position in the shop. Products at eye level sell noticeably better than the same products placed near the floor, and manufacturers often pay for the best positions. Goods intended for children, such as sweets and some breakfast cereals, are sometimes placed lower down, where young eyes will find them. The ends of aisles, which shoppers see as they turn, are especially valuable, and items placed there can sell several times as quickly as they do in the middle of a shelf, even when the price is unchanged. Many shoppers assume that goods displayed in this way are on special offer, although often they are not.
paragraphs.label: D

paragraphs.text: Researchers who study shoppers have found that most people move through a store in a broadly similar pattern, often travelling around the outside first and entering only some of the central aisles. In many countries shoppers also tend to move anticlockwise, although the reasons for this are debated. Stores use this knowledge to decide where to put the products that people plan to buy and where to put those they are likely to pick up on impulse. The aim is not so much to trap customers as to expose them to as many products as possible in the time they are willing to spend. Large chains often test a new layout in a small number of branches first, measuring how long customers stay and how much they spend before introducing it everywhere.
paragraphs.label: E

paragraphs.text: Some popular beliefs about supermarkets are harder to support. It is often said that stores pump the smell of fresh bread into their aisles to make people hungry, but in most cases the smell simply comes from an in-store bakery that exists to sell bread. Similarly, the claim that music is deliberately slowed down to make shoppers linger rests on a small number of studies carried out decades ago, and later attempts to repeat the findings have produced mixed results. Such stories spread because they are memorable, not because they have been well tested.
paragraphs.label: F

paragraphs.text: Layouts are also changing. The growth of online ordering means that a large part of some stores is now visited by staff picking items for delivery, who want products arranged for speed rather than for temptation. Smaller convenience shops, which many people use for a few items on the way home, put essentials near the door because their customers will simply go elsewhere if a quick visit takes too long. In these shops, the long walk to the milk would be a disadvantage rather than a sales technique. Some large stores have responded by opening a small section near the entrance for the items most often bought on quick visits.
paragraphs.label: G

paragraphs.text: None of this means that shoppers are powerless. A written list, a basket instead of a trolley and a clear idea of what is needed all reduce the amount that people spend beyond their plans, and several studies suggest that shoppers who eat before visiting a supermarket buy fewer items they did not intend to buy. The layout of a shop is designed to influence behaviour, but it works mainly on people who are not paying attention. Understanding how it works is, in the end, the most effective defence against it, and it costs nothing.
paragraphs.label: H

topic.en: A general-interest text: how supermarket layouts are planned, and which explanations are true and which are myths.
topic.kk: Жалпы қызығушылық мәтіні: супермаркеттің орналасуы қалай ойластырылған және оның қай түсіндірмесі дұрыс, қайсысы аңыз.
topic.ru: Текст общего интереса: как устроена планировка супермаркета и какие объяснения этому верны, а какие — мифы.

items.quote: Putting dairy products along the rear wall shortens the distance that heavy, chilled deliveries have to travel
items.prompt: a reason for the position of dairy products that is connected with deliveries

explanation.en: “shortens the distance that heavy, chilled deliveries have to travel” → C: dairy is at the back to shorten deliveries.
explanation.kk: «shortens the distance that heavy, chilled deliveries have to travel» → C: сүт өнімдері жеткізу жолы қысқа болу үшін артқы қабырғада тұр.
explanation.ru: «shortens the distance that heavy, chilled deliveries have to travel» → C: молочные продукты у задней стены ради коротких поставок.

items.quote: put essentials near the door because their customers will simply go elsewhere if a quick visit takes too long
items.prompt: an example of shops that are arranged for customers in a hurry

explanation.en: “put essentials near the door because… a quick visit takes too long” → G: small convenience shops.
explanation.kk: «put essentials near the door because… a quick visit takes too long» → G: үй жанындағы шағын дүкендер.
explanation.ru: «put essentials near the door because… a quick visit takes too long» → G: маленькие магазины у дома.

items.quote: later attempts to repeat the findings have produced mixed results
items.prompt: a claim about shop design that later research has not clearly confirmed

explanation.en: “later attempts to repeat the findings have produced mixed results” → F: the slow-music story.
explanation.kk: «later attempts to repeat the findings have produced mixed results» → F: баяу музыка туралы әңгіме.
explanation.ru: «later attempts to repeat the findings have produced mixed results» → F: история про медленную музыку.

items.quote: The ends of aisles, which shoppers see as they turn, are especially valuable
items.prompt: the value of a place that customers notice as they change direction

explanation.en: “The ends of aisles, which shoppers see as they turn, are especially valuable” → D. “Change direction” = “turn”. Moving anticlockwise (E) is not about a spot on the shelf.
explanation.kk: «The ends of aisles, which shoppers see as they turn, are especially valuable» → D. «Change direction» мен «turn» — бір мағына. E-дегі сағат тіліне қарсы жүру сөре туралы емес.
explanation.ru: «The ends of aisles, which shoppers see as they turn, are especially valuable» → D. «Change direction» = «turn». Движение против часовой стрелки (E) — не про место на полке.

groups.instruction: The text has eight paragraphs, A–H. Which paragraph contains the following information? Write the correct letter, A–H.

items.quote: Many shoppers assume that this is a trick, and to some extent they are right.
items.prompt: Shoppers who suspect the long walk to the milk is planned are partly correct.

explanation.en: “to some extent they are right” → YES: the writer partly agrees.
explanation.kk: «to some extent they are right» → YES: автор сатып алушылармен ішінара келіседі.
explanation.ru: «to some extent they are right» → YES: автор частично согласен с покупателями.

items.quote: Products placed right by the door are often ignored
items.prompt: The area just inside the entrance is the best place for goods a shop wants to promote.

explanation.en: “Products placed right by the door are often ignored” → NO: that space is used for seasonal displays instead.
explanation.kk: «Products placed right by the door are often ignored» → NO: есік алдындағы тауарды байқамайды, сондықтан онда маусымдық сөре тұрады.
explanation.ru: «Products placed right by the door are often ignored» → NO: у самого входа товары не замечают, поэтому там сезонные витрины.

items.quote: There is some truth in this, but there is also a practical reason that is rarely mentioned.
items.prompt: The practical reason for keeping milk at the back matters more to stores than the commercial one.

explanation.en: The writer gives both reasons (“some truth” and “also a practical reason”) but never says which matters more → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Автор екі себепті де атайды («some truth» және «also a practical reason»), бірақ қайсысы маңыздырақ екенін айтпайды → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Автор называет обе причины («some truth» и «also a practical reason»), но не говорит, какая важнее → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: The aim is not so much to trap customers as to expose them to as many products as possible
items.prompt: The main purpose of store layouts is to stop customers from leaving.

explanation.en: “The aim is not so much to trap customers as to expose them to as many products as possible” → NO.
explanation.kk: «The aim is not so much to trap customers as to expose them to as many products as possible» → NO: мақсат — ұстап қалу емес, көбірек тауар көрсету.
explanation.ru: «The aim is not so much to trap customers as to expose them to as many products as possible» → NO: цель — показать больше товаров, а не удержать.

items.quote: the claim that music is deliberately slowed down to make shoppers linger rests on a small number of studies carried out decades ago
items.prompt: Supermarkets that play slow music earn more than those that do not.

explanation.en: The writer says the slow-music evidence is old and mixed; store earnings are never discussed → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Автор баяу музыка туралы дерек ескі әрі даулы дейді; дүкен табысы туралы ештеңе айтылмаған → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Автор говорит, что данные о медленной музыке старые и спорные; о доходах магазинов ничего не сказано → NOT GIVEN.

groups.instruction: Do the following statements agree with the claims of the writer in the text? Write YES if the statement agrees with the claims of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the claims of the writer, NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.

items.quote: Products at eye level sell noticeably better than the same products placed near the floor
items.prompt: Items shown at ____ outsell identical items at the bottom of the shelves.

explanation.en: “Products at eye level sell noticeably better than the same products placed near the floor” → eye level.
explanation.kk: «Products at eye level sell noticeably better than the same products placed near the floor» → eye level: көз деңгейіндегі тауар жақсы өтеді.
explanation.ru: «Products at eye level sell noticeably better than the same products placed near the floor» → eye level.

items.quote: In many countries shoppers also tend to move anticlockwise
items.prompt: In many countries, people usually go round a store in an ____ direction.

explanation.en: “shoppers also tend to move anticlockwise” → anticlockwise, written as one word.
explanation.kk: «shoppers also tend to move anticlockwise» → anticlockwise. Емлесіне назар аударыңыз: бірге жазылған бір сөз.
explanation.ru: «shoppers also tend to move anticlockwise» → anticlockwise. Слово пишется слитно.

items.quote: who want products arranged for speed rather than for temptation
items.prompt: Staff who collect online orders want goods to be arranged for ____.

explanation.en: “who want products arranged for speed rather than for temptation” → speed; “temptation” is what they do not want.
explanation.kk: «who want products arranged for speed rather than for temptation» → speed; «temptation» — оларға керегі жоқ нәрсе.
explanation.ru: «who want products arranged for speed rather than for temptation» → speed; «temptation» — то, чего им как раз не нужно.

groups.instruction: Complete the sentences below. Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the text for each answer.

items.quote: in most cases the smell simply comes from an in-store bakery that exists to sell bread
items.prompt: What does the writer say about the smell of bread in supermarkets?

options.text: It is pumped into the aisles to make people hungry.
It usually comes from bread that is really baked in the shop.
It has been proved to increase sales.
It is found mainly in smaller shops.

explanation.en: “in most cases the smell simply comes from an in-store bakery” → B. Option A is the popular belief the writer rejects.
explanation.kk: «in most cases the smell simply comes from an in-store bakery» → B. A нұсқасы — автор жоққа шығаратын кең таралған аңыз.
explanation.ru: «in most cases the smell simply comes from an in-store bakery» → B. Вариант A — популярный миф, который автор опровергает.

items.quote: it works mainly on people who are not paying attention
items.prompt: What is the writer’s main conclusion?

options.text: Shoppers cannot resist the influence of store layouts.
Store layouts mostly affect shoppers who are not attentive.
Supermarkets should be required to change their layouts.
Online ordering will soon make store layouts unimportant.

explanation.en: “it works mainly on people who are not paying attention” → B. A goes too far: the writer says shoppers are not powerless.
explanation.kk: «it works mainly on people who are not paying attention» → B. A тым күшті: автор сатып алушылар дәрменсіз емес дейді.
explanation.ru: «it works mainly on people who are not paying attention» → B. A слишком сильно: автор прямо пишет, что покупатели не беспомощны.

groups.instruction: Choose the correct letter, A, B, C or D.
